⏺ # Runway display-logic gap: multi-day rows render twice

  ## What I observed

  `Policy Materials Import (LPPC)` (id `63e4aeab1d6d47449458e9d5b`) appears in two places on the board today:

  1. Under `This Week` -> `Mon 4/27` — placed by `startDate=2026-04-27`
  2. Presumably also under In Flight / Today — placed because the row is actively spanning today

  Same row, same data, two visual locations. Confirmed via screenshot from the board.

  ## Data state is correct

  The row is a faithful multi-day representation. Per Kathy's 2026-04-28 audit, work began ~4/24 (policy materials added
  to CMS) and continues through 5/4 (Leslie tagging in CMS). Current shape:

  - `startDate` = 2026-04-27
  - `date` = 2026-05-04
  - `endDate` = 2026-05-04
  - `weekOf` = 2026-05-04
  - `dayOfWeek` = monday
  - `category` = kickoff
  - `status` = in-progress

  Convention is satisfied: multi-day, `date` mirrors `endDate`, `weekOf` is Monday of date's week. No data correction
  needed.

  ## The bug is in the renderer

  The board's `This Week` section appears to anchor multi-day items on their `startDate`'s day cell. Once `startDate <=
  today`, the row should leave the day-anchored `This Week` placement and live in active-state sections only. That isn't
  happening. Net effect: every multi-day row that crosses today renders twice.

  This affects more than just LPPC. Any active multi-day L2 across the system has the same artifact.

  ## Desired behavior

  Three placement zones, mutually exclusive for a given row at a given point in time:

  | Zone | Match rule |
  |---|---|
  | **Today** | `startDate <= today <= endDate` AND `status != completed/canceled` |
  | **In Flight** | Same condition as Today, but for the broader "what's actively spanning" surface (likely the same set,
   different visual treatment) |
  | **This Week** day cells | Single-day rows where `date == today's week` AND status is scheduled, OR multi-day rows
  where `startDate > today` (haven't started yet, anchored on startDate's day for forecast visibility) |

  Once `startDate` has passed, the day-anchored `This Week` row disappears. Replaced by Today + In Flight presence.

  # R1 Thought Partner brief: Slack-bot modal trigger for net-new entity creation

  ## What the operator wants

  When someone in Slack DM-converses with the Runway bot in natural language and the bot decides this input means "create
   a NEW retainer wrapper, NEW L1 project, or NEW L2 week_item," surface a Slack modal first. User confirms / fills
  missing fields / cancels in the modal; the write only fires after submit.

  Modal scope: net-new creates only (not updates). Three target entities: wrapper, L1, L2.

  ## Current pipeline (verified from code, file:line refs included)

  ### Intent classification
  - Pure LLM tool-calling via Vercel AI SDK's `generateText`, model `claude-haiku-4-5-20251001`.
  - `src/lib/slack/bot.ts:204-210` — `generateText({ model, messages, tools, stopWhen: stepCountIs(MAX_STEPS=12),
  maxRetries: 1 })`.
  - Slack DM → `/api/slack/events/route.ts:115-125` enqueues Inngest → `inngest/functions/runway-slack-message.ts:48`
  calls `handleDirectMessage` → spawns the LLM tool loop.
  - No regex, no rules-based router, no separate classifier. The model emits `toolCalls` and the dispatch happens inside
  the AI-SDK loop.

  ### Create-vs-update decision
  - Lives entirely in the LLM's prompt-driven choice between `create_*` and `update_*` tool names.
  - The "policy" is text in `src/lib/runway/bot-context-behaviors.ts:67-85,96-125` — confirmation rules, ambiguity
  guidance, "Sound right?" prompt before creating a project — purely instruction to the model, NOT enforced anywhere in
  code.
  - `src/lib/slack/bot.ts:223-238` only LOGS tool calls AFTER they execute. There's no pre-write hook today.

  ### Tool surface (bot-tools.ts)
  | Create-side | Update-side |
  |---|---|
  | `create_project` (line 261) | `update_project_status`, `update_project_field` |
  | `create_week_item` (line 369) | `update_week_item` |
  | `create_pipeline_item` (line 527) | `update_pipeline_item` |
  | `create_team_member` (line 611) | `update_team_member`, `update_client_field` |

  Plus `add_update` (note-only, not a write), `undo_last_change`, three `delete_*`.

  ### Wrapper creation is broken at the bot layer
  - A "wrapper" needs `engagementType="retainer"` + `parentProjectId=null` + child L1s linked.
  - Bot's `create_project` (`bot-tools.ts:264-273`) does NOT expose `engagementType`, `parentProjectId`, `contractStart`,
   or `contractEnd`. It only takes `clientSlug, name, status, owner, resources, dueDate, waitingOn, notes`.
  - `update_project_field`'s field enum (`bot-tools.ts:315-323`) excludes `engagementType` entirely.
  - MCP's `add_project` (`runway-tools.ts:512-527`) and the underlying `addProject` operation (`operations-add.ts:36-49`)
   DO expose all the wrapper fields. The bot is the bottleneck.
  - Net effect: the bot literally cannot create a retainer wrapper today. Modal work needs to either fix this gap first
  or accept that "wrapper" is an MCP/data-tp-only path.

  ### Modal scaffolding state
  - ZERO. Grep for `views.open|modal|interactivity|block_actions|view_submission` across `src/` returns no Slack-modal
  hits.
  - No `/api/slack/interactivity` route. Slack signature verification exists in `src/lib/slack/verify.ts` (reusable).
  Slack client at `src/lib/slack/client.ts` is currently used for `chat.postMessage` only.

  ### The hard architectural problem
  - `generateText`'s `execute:` callback inside each `tool({ ... })` definition runs inside the LLM loop. It must resolve
   a result before `generateText` proceeds.
  - A modal-gated flow can't just "pause" the loop and wait for user submit — Vercel AI SDK doesn't support resumable
  tool calls in this shape.
  - Realistic shape: when an `execute` callback for a `create_*` tool fires, it stores the proposed args server-side,
  opens a Slack modal, returns a "modal opened, awaiting confirmation" result to the LLM (which will likely respond to
  user "I've opened a confirmation modal"), and TERMINATES the run. On modal submit, a new `/api/slack/interactivity`
  handler picks up the stored args and invokes the underlying `addProject` / `createWeekItem` directly (bypassing the LLM
   round-trip).

  ### Disambiguation gaps that affect modal scope
  - Per `bot-context-behaviors.ts:80-85`, ambiguity is resolved by prompt instruction (LLM asks). Examples don't cover
  create-vs-update specifically.
  - "Add a follow-up for Convergix" likely defaults to `create_week_item` — no instruction to first search for existing
  matches.
  - `addProject` blocks exact-normalized duplicate names (`operations-add.ts:106`), but close-but-not-equal names would
  slip through.
  - A modal could also be a disambiguation surface: "We found 3 similar existing items. Update one, or create new?"

  ## Design questions for thought-partner

  1. **Architectural shape.** Confirm or refine the proposed flow: `execute` callback for `create_*` opens a modal +
  terminates the LLM run + stores proposed args (where? Inngest event payload, KV, DB row?). On modal submit, a fresh
  handler dispatches the create. Identify the failure modes (what if user dismisses the modal? Where does the
  conversation thread state live? Is there a TTL on stored proposals?).

  2. **Wrapper-creation gap.** Is the right move to (a) extend bot's `create_project` to accept
  `engagementType`/`parentProjectId`/`contractStart`/`contractEnd`, then build the modal on top of the unified tool, OR
  (b) leave wrapper creation as MCP/data-tp-only and skip modal-for-wrapper, OR (c) add a dedicated
  `create_retainer_wrapper` bot tool that is modal-gated by default? Trade-offs?

  3. **Modal as disambiguation gate.** Should the modal trigger ALSO fire when input is ambiguous between create and
  update (e.g., proposes "Update existing X (90% match)" vs "Create new" toggles)? Or strictly net-new only?

  4. **Update path.** Operator scoped this to creates. But are there high-impact UPDATES that should also gate behind a
  modal (status changes on multi-month projects, parent_project_id assignments, contract date changes)? Surface as a
  follow-on, don't fold in.

  5. **Slack interactivity stack.** New route at `/api/slack/interactivity`, signature verify, modal definition format
  (Block Kit), state-passing between LLM proposal and modal submit. Identify reusable parts of existing `bot-tools.ts`
  argument validation so the modal handler shares the same write-path.

  6. **What does "create signal" mean concretely.** The bot today decides `create_*` purely from prompt text. Do you want
   to keep that LLM-driven? Or add a deterministic pre-LLM classifier (regex / keyword / lookup) that flags "this looks
  like a create" before the LLM picks a tool? Implications for false-positive modal pops.

  7. **Confirm the resumable-flow assumption.** I claimed `generateText` can't pause and resume. Verify against current
  AI SDK v6 docs — there may be a streaming-tool-result pattern that allows it. If yes, the architecture changes
  substantially.

  ## Out of scope for this brief
  - Data corrections (data-tp's swimlane).
  - The display-logic bug separately filed (multi-day rows rendering twice).
  - Auth / WorkOS layer changes.
  - Production deployment plan (Runway deploys from runway branch already; no Vercel preview gate).

  ## Reference files (hydration list)
  - `src/lib/slack/bot.ts` — main loop, model config, MAX_STEPS, MUTATION_TOOLS list.
  - `src/lib/slack/bot-tools.ts` — all tool definitions with `execute:` callbacks. Modal injection points live here.
  - `src/lib/runway/bot-context-behaviors.ts` — system-prompt instructions (intent guidance lives here).
  - `src/lib/runway/bot-context.ts`, `bot-context-sections.ts` — system prompt assembly.
  - `src/lib/mcp/runway-tools.ts` — MCP tool registry (compare full surface vs bot's restricted surface).
  - `src/lib/runway/operations-add.ts`, `operations-writes-project.ts` — underlying write helpers (modal handler will
  call these directly post-submit).
  - `src/app/api/slack/events/route.ts` — Slack event ingress, signature verify pattern.
  - `src/lib/inngest/functions/runway-slack-message.ts` — Inngest function that owns the conversation lifecycle.
  - `src/lib/slack/verify.ts` — Slack signature verification helper.
  - `src/lib/slack/client.ts` — Slack Web API client.

  ## What I'm asking for back
  A staged plan: (1) close the wrapper-creation gap, (2) ship `/api/slack/interactivity` infra + a working modal for one
  `create_*` path as proof of pattern, (3) extend to all four create paths + wrapper, (4) optionally extend to
  disambiguation. Each stage with code-level direction CC can act on.

  Paste-ready. Drops thought-partner straight into the architecture seam without re-discovery overhead.

⏺ All 6 warnings are false positives. The detector is checking dayOfWeek and weekOf against startDate when the convention
   (per the intent doc) ties both fields to date, not startDate.

  Verification against prod

  Row: R3 Design Review
  Field: dayOfWeek=thursday
  Prod state: date=4/23 (Thu), startDate=4/20 (Mon)
  Convention check: 4/23 is Thursday → match ✓
  Detector said: "dayOfWeek 'thursday' doesn't match 2026-04-20 (monday)" — checks startDate
  Reality: False positive
  ────────────────────────────────────────
  Row: Development Kickoff
  Field: dayOfWeek=thursday
  Prod state: date=4/23 (Thu), startDate=4/20 (Mon)
  Convention check: Same as above ✓
  Detector said: Same wrong-field check
  Reality: False positive
  ────────────────────────────────────────
  Row: Pencils Down
  Field: dayOfWeek=monday
  Prod state: date=5/4 (Mon), startDate=4/23 (Thu)
  Convention check: 5/4 is Monday → match ✓
  Detector said: "dayOfWeek 'monday' doesn't match 2026-04-23 (thursday)" — checks startDate
  Reality: False positive
  ────────────────────────────────────────
  Row: QA Phase
  Field: dayOfWeek=friday
  Prod state: date=5/8 (Fri), startDate=5/7 (Thu)
  Convention check: 5/8 is Friday → match ✓
  Detector said: "dayOfWeek 'friday' doesn't match 2026-05-07 (thursday)" — checks startDate
  Reality: False positive
  ────────────────────────────────────────
  Row: Pencils Down
  Field: weekOf=2026-05-04
  Prod state: date=5/4, startDate=4/23
  Convention check: Monday(date)=5/4 → match ✓
  Detector said: "weekOf '2026-05-04' isn't Monday-of-week for 2026-04-23 (expected 2026-04-20)" — checks startDate's
  week
  Reality: False positive
  ────────────────────────────────────────
  Row: Policy Materials Import
  Field: weekOf=2026-05-04
  Prod state: date=5/4, startDate=4/27
  Convention check: Monday(date)=5/4 → match ✓
  Detector said: "weekOf '2026-05-04' isn't Monday-of-week for 2026-04-27 (expected 2026-04-27)" — checks startDate's
  week
  Reality: False positive

  Convention reference (intent doc, lines 17-20)

  ▎ date mirrors endDate on multi-day range tasks.
  ▎ dayOfWeek tracks date (not startDate).
  ▎ weekOf is the Monday of the week containing date.

  The mechanical sweep we just ran enforced exactly this — date=endDate, dayOfWeek=Monday-of-date's-day-of-week,
  weekOf=Monday(date). Every row the Gantt flagged is convention-clean.

  Why the detector is wrong

  The Gantt TP's detector is reading startDate as the anchor for dayOfWeek and weekOf checks. That would be correct under
   a different convention ("dayOfWeek tracks startDate") but the project picked the opposite — date is the canonical
  anchor for both, and date == endDate on multi-day items.

  For single-day rows (startDate == date == endDate) the detector accidentally produces correct results because all three
   fields agree. The bug only surfaces on multi-day items — which is exactly what the Gantt is showing.

  Fix direction (when you brief the Gantt TP)

  Detector check should be:

  const expectedDayOfWeek = dayName(row.date);          // not row.startDate
  const expectedWeekOf = mondayOf(row.date);            // not mondayOf(row.startDate)

  And the convention reference for whoever owns it: docs/runway-data-integrity-intent.md lines 17-20.

  Other observations from the Gantt

  The visual itself is clean — milestones (LPPC Images Due, Hero Video Resolution, Staging Links Due, etc.) render
  correctly as diamonds. Active multi-day bars (Pencils Down 4/23-5/4, Policy Materials Import 4/27-5/4, QA Phase
  5/7-5/8) render correctly. The display layer is doing the right thing; only the integrity detector is mis-aligned.

  LPPC Website Revamp data is clean — the Gantt's "5 of 12 rows have data gaps" is a false alarm.

  ## What I observed

  `Policy Materials Import (LPPC)` (id `63e4aeab1d6d47449458e9d5b`) appears in two places on the board today:

  1. Under `This Week` -> `Mon 4/27` — placed by `startDate=2026-04-27`

  ## Data state is correct

  The row is a faithful multi-day representation. Per Kathy's 2026-04-28 audit, work began ~4/24 (policy materials added
   to CMS) and continues through 5/4 (Leslie tagging in CMS). Current shape:

  - `startDate` = 2026-04-27

  - `endDate` = 2026-05-04

  - `dayOfWeek` = monday
  - `category` = kickoff
  - `status` = in-progress

  Convention is satisfied: multi-day, `date` mirrors `endDate`, `weekOf` is Monday of date's week. No data correction
  needed.

  ## The bug is in the renderer

  The board's `This Week` section appears to anchor multi-day items on their `startDate`'s day cell. Once `startDate <=
  today`, the row should leave the day-anchored `This Week` placement and live in active-state sections only. That isn't
   happening. Net effect: every multi-day row that crosses today renders twice.

  This affects more than just LPPC. Any active multi-day L2 across the system has the same artifact.

  ## Desired behavior

  Three placement zones, mutually exclusive for a given row at a given point in time:

  | Zone | Match rule |
  |---|---|
  | **Today** | `startDate <= today <= endDate` AND `status != completed/canceled` |
  | **In Flight** | Same condition as Today, but for the broader "what's actively spanning" surface (likely the same
  set, different visual treatment) |
  | **This Week** day cells | Single-day rows where `date == today's week` AND status is scheduled, OR multi-day rows
  where `startDate > today` (haven't started yet, anchored on startDate's day for forecast visibility) |

  Once `startDate` has passed, the day-anchored `This Week` row disappears. Replaced by Today + In Flight presence.

  Future-dated multi-day rows still anchor on startDate's day in `This Week` — so users can see "kickoff Wed of next
  week" before the work starts. The disappearance trigger is `startDate <= today`.

  # R1 Thought Partner brief: Slack-bot modal trigger for net-new entity creation

  ## What the operator wants

  When someone in Slack DM-converses with the Runway bot in natural language and the bot decides this input means
  "create a NEW retainer wrapper, NEW L1 project, or NEW L2 week_item," surface a Slack modal first. User confirms /
  fills missing fields / cancels in the modal; the write only fires after submit.

  Modal scope: net-new creates only (not updates). Three target entities: wrapper, L1, L2.

  ## Current pipeline (verified from code, file:line refs included)

  ### Intent classification
  - Pure LLM tool-calling via Vercel AI SDK's `generateText`, model `claude-haiku-4-5-20251001`.
  - `src/lib/slack/bot.ts:204-210` — `generateText({ model, messages, tools, stopWhen: stepCountIs(MAX_STEPS=12),
  maxRetries: 1 })`.
  - Slack DM → `/api/slack/events/route.ts:115-125` enqueues Inngest → `inngest/functions/runway-slack-message.ts:48`
  calls `handleDirectMessage` → spawns the LLM tool loop.
  - No regex, no rules-based router, no separate classifier. The model emits `toolCalls` and the dispatch happens inside
   the AI-SDK loop.

  ### Create-vs-update decision
  - Lives entirely in the LLM's prompt-driven choice between `create_*` and `update_*` tool names.
  - The "policy" is text in `src/lib/runway/bot-context-behaviors.ts:67-85,96-125` — confirmation rules, ambiguity
  guidance, "Sound right?" prompt before creating a project — purely instruction to the model, NOT enforced anywhere in
  code.
  - `src/lib/slack/bot.ts:223-238` only LOGS tool calls AFTER they execute. There's no pre-write hook today.

  ### Tool surface (bot-tools.ts)
  | Create-side | Update-side |
  |---|---|
  | `create_project` (line 261) | `update_project_status`, `update_project_field` |
  | `create_week_item` (line 369) | `update_week_item` |
  | `create_pipeline_item` (line 527) | `update_pipeline_item` |
  | `create_team_member` (line 611) | `update_team_member`, `update_client_field` |

  Plus `add_update` (note-only, not a write), `undo_last_change`, three `delete_*`.

  ### Wrapper creation is broken at the bot layer
  - A "wrapper" needs `engagementType="retainer"` + `parentProjectId=null` + child L1s linked.
  - Bot's `create_project` (`bot-tools.ts:264-273`) does NOT expose `engagementType`, `parentProjectId`,
  `contractStart`, or `contractEnd`. It only takes `clientSlug, name, status, owner, resources, dueDate, waitingOn,
  notes`.
  - `update_project_field`'s field enum (`bot-tools.ts:315-323`) excludes `engagementType` entirely.
  - MCP's `add_project` (`runway-tools.ts:512-527`) and the underlying `addProject` operation
  (`operations-add.ts:36-49`) DO expose all the wrapper fields. The bot is the bottleneck.
  - Net effect: the bot literally cannot create a retainer wrapper today. Modal work needs to either fix this gap first
  or accept that "wrapper" is an MCP/data-tp-only path.

  ### Modal scaffolding state
  - ZERO. Grep for `views.open|modal|interactivity|block_actions|view_submission` across `src/` returns no Slack-modal
  hits.
  - No `/api/slack/interactivity` route. Slack signature verification exists in `src/lib/slack/verify.ts` (reusable).
  Slack client at `src/lib/slack/client.ts` is currently used for `chat.postMessage` only.

  ### The hard architectural problem
  - `generateText`'s `execute:` callback inside each `tool({ ... })` definition runs inside the LLM loop. It must
  resolve a result before `generateText` proceeds.
  - A modal-gated flow can't just "pause" the loop and wait for user submit — Vercel AI SDK doesn't support resumable
  tool calls in this shape.
  - Realistic shape: when an `execute` callback for a `create_*` tool fires, it stores the proposed args server-side,
  opens a Slack modal, returns a "modal opened, awaiting confirmation" result to the LLM (which will likely respond to
  user "I've opened a confirmation modal"), and TERMINATES the run. On modal submit, a new `/api/slack/interactivity`
  handler picks up the stored args and invokes the underlying `addProject` / `createWeekItem` directly (bypassing the
  LLM round-trip).

  ### Disambiguation gaps that affect modal scope
  - Per `bot-context-behaviors.ts:80-85`, ambiguity is resolved by prompt instruction (LLM asks). Examples don't cover
  create-vs-update specifically.
  - "Add a follow-up for Convergix" likely defaults to `create_week_item` — no instruction to first search for existing
  matches.
  - `addProject` blocks exact-normalized duplicate names (`operations-add.ts:106`), but close-but-not-equal names would
  slip through.
  - A modal could also be a disambiguation surface: "We found 3 similar existing items. Update one, or create new?"

  ## Design questions for thought-partner

  1. **Architectural shape.** Confirm or refine the proposed flow: `execute` callback for `create_*` opens a modal +
  terminates the LLM run + stores proposed args (where? Inngest event payload, KV, DB row?). On modal submit, a fresh
  handler dispatches the create. Identify the failure modes (what if user dismisses the modal? Where does the
  conversation thread state live? Is there a TTL on stored proposals?).

  2. **Wrapper-creation gap.** Is the right move to (a) extend bot's `create_project` to accept
  `engagementType`/`parentProjectId`/`contractStart`/`contractEnd`, then build the modal on top of the unified tool, OR
  (b) leave wrapper creation as MCP/data-tp-only and skip modal-for-wrapper, OR (c) add a dedicated
  `create_retainer_wrapper` bot tool that is modal-gated by default? Trade-offs?

  3. **Modal as disambiguation gate.** Should the modal trigger ALSO fire when input is ambiguous between create and
  update (e.g., proposes "Update existing X (90% match)" vs "Create new" toggles)? Or strictly net-new only?

  4. **Update path.** Operator scoped this to creates. But are there high-impact UPDATES that should also gate behind a
  modal (status changes on multi-month projects, parent_project_id assignments, contract date changes)? Surface as a
  follow-on, don't fold in.

  5. **Slack interactivity stack.** New route at `/api/slack/interactivity`, signature verify, modal definition format
  (Block Kit), state-passing between LLM proposal and modal submit. Identify reusable parts of existing `bot-tools.ts`
  argument validation so the modal handler shares the same write-path.

  6. **What does "create signal" mean concretely.** The bot today decides `create_*` purely from prompt text. Do you
  want to keep that LLM-driven? Or add a deterministic pre-LLM classifier (regex / keyword / lookup) that flags "this
  looks like a create" before the LLM picks a tool? Implications for false-positive modal pops.

  7. **Confirm the resumable-flow assumption.** I claimed `generateText` can't pause and resume. Verify against current
  AI SDK v6 docs — there may be a streaming-tool-result pattern that allows it. If yes, the architecture changes
  substantially.

  ## Out of scope for this brief
  - Data corrections (data-tp's swimlane).
  - The display-logic bug separately filed (multi-day rows rendering twice).
  - Auth / WorkOS layer changes.
  - Production deployment plan (Runway deploys from runway branch already; no Vercel preview gate).

  ## Reference files (hydration list)
  - `src/lib/slack/bot.ts` — main loop, model config, MAX_STEPS, MUTATION_TOOLS list.
  - `src/lib/slack/bot-tools.ts` — all tool definitions with `execute:` callbacks. Modal injection points live here.
  - `src/lib/runway/bot-context-behaviors.ts` — system-prompt instructions (intent guidance lives here).
  - `src/lib/runway/bot-context.ts`, `bot-context-sections.ts` — system prompt assembly.
  - `src/lib/mcp/runway-tools.ts` — MCP tool registry (compare full surface vs bot's restricted surface).
  - `src/lib/runway/operations-add.ts`, `operations-writes-project.ts` — underlying write helpers (modal handler will
  call these directly post-submit).
  - `src/app/api/slack/events/route.ts` — Slack event ingress, signature verify pattern.
  - `src/lib/inngest/functions/runway-slack-message.ts` — Inngest function that owns the conversation lifecycle.
  - `src/lib/slack/verify.ts` — Slack signature verification helper.
  - `src/lib/slack/client.ts` — Slack Web API client.

  ## What I'm asking for back
  A staged plan: (1) close the wrapper-creation gap, (2) ship `/api/slack/interactivity` infra + a working modal for one
   `create_*` path as proof of pattern, (3) extend to all four create paths + wrapper, (4) optionally extend to
  disambiguation. Each stage with code-level direction CC can act on.

  Paste-ready. Drops thought-partner straight into the architecture seam without re-discovery overhead.

    week
  Reality: False positive

  Row: Policy Materials Import
  Field: weekOf=2026-05-04
  Prod state: date=5/4, startDate=4/27
  Convention check: Monday(date)=5/4 → match ✓

    week
  Reality: False positive

  Convention reference (intent doc, lines 17-20)

  ▎ date mirrors endDate on multi-day range tasks.
  ▎ dayOfWeek tracks date (not startDate).
  ▎ weekOf is the Monday of the week containing date.

  The mechanical sweep we just ran enforced exactly this — date=endDate, dayOfWeek=Monday-of-date's-day-of-week,
  weekOf=Monday(date). Every row the Gantt flagged is convention-clean.

  Why the detector is wrong

  The Gantt TP's detector is reading startDate as the anchor for dayOfWeek and weekOf checks. That would be correct
  under a different convention ("dayOfWeek tracks startDate") but the project picked the opposite — date is the
  canonical anchor for both, and date == endDate on multi-day items.

  For single-day rows (startDate == date == endDate) the detector accidentally produces correct results because all
  three fields agree. The bug only surfaces on multi-day items — which is exactly what the Gantt is showing.

  Fix direction (when you brief the Gantt TP)

  Detector check should be:

  const expectedDayOfWeek = dayName(row.date);          // not row.startDate
  const expectedWeekOf = mondayOf(row.date);            // not mondayOf(row.startDate)

  And the convention reference for whoever owns it: docs/runway-data-integrity-intent.md lines 17-20.

  Other observations from the Gantt

  The visual itself is clean — milestones (LPPC Images Due, Hero Video Resolution, Staging Links Due, etc.) render
  correctly as diamonds. Active multi-day bars (Pencils Down 4/23-5/4, Policy Materials Import 4/27-5/4, QA Phase
  5/7-5/8) render correctly. The display layer is doing the right thing; only the integrity detector is mis-aligned.

  LPPC Website Revamp data is clean — the Gantt's "5 of 12 rows have data gaps" is a false alarm.

⏺ # Runway display-logic gap: multi-day rows render twice

  ## What I observed

  `Policy Materials Import (LPPC)` (id `63e4aeab1d6d47449458e9d5b`) appears in two places on the board today:

  1. Under `This Week` -> `Mon 4/27` — placed by `startDate=2026-04-27`
  2. Presumably also under In Flight / Today — placed because the row is actively spanning today

  Same row, same data, two visual locations. Confirmed via screenshot from the board.

  ## Data state is correct

  The row is a faithful multi-day representation. Per Kathy's 2026-04-28 audit, work began ~4/24 (policy materials added
   to CMS) and continues through 5/4 (Leslie tagging in CMS). Current shape:

  - `startDate` = 2026-04-27
  - `date` = 2026-05-04
  - `endDate` = 2026-05-04
  - `weekOf` = 2026-05-04
  - `dayOfWeek` = monday
  - `category` = kickoff
  - `status` = in-progress

  Convention is satisfied: multi-day, `date` mirrors `endDate`, `weekOf` is Monday of date's week. No data correction
  needed.

  ## The bug is in the renderer

  The board's `This Week` section appears to anchor multi-day items on their `startDate`'s day cell. Once `startDate <=
  today`, the row should leave the day-anchored `This Week` placement and live in active-state sections only. That isn't
   happening. Net effect: every multi-day row that crosses today renders twice.

  This affects more than just LPPC. Any active multi-day L2 across the system has the same artifact.

  ## Desired behavior

  Three placement zones, mutually exclusive for a given row at a given point in time:

  | Zone | Match rule |
  |---|---|
  | **Today** | `startDate <= today <= endDate` AND `status != completed/canceled` |
  | **In Flight** | Same condition as Today, but for the broader "what's actively spanning" surface (likely the same
  set, different visual treatment) |
  | **This Week** day cells | Single-day rows where `date == today's week` AND status is scheduled, OR multi-day rows
  where `startDate > today` (haven't started yet, anchored on startDate's day for forecast visibility) |

  Once `startDate` has passed, the day-anchored `This Week` row disappears. Replaced by Today + In Flight presence.

  Future-dated multi-day rows still anchor on startDate's day in `This Week` — so users can see "kickoff Wed of next
  week" before the work starts. The disappearance trigger is `startDate <= today`.

  ## Repro case

  Pull `Policy Materials Import (LPPC)` weekItem from prod. Render the board. Observe duplicate placement: Mon 4/27 in
  `This Week` AND wherever active spans render. Today is 2026-04-29, startDate is 2026-04-27, so the row is
  past-startDate.

  After fix, the Mon 4/27 placement should be gone; only Today + In Flight render this row.

  ## Other multi-day rows likely affected (LPPC scope, fresh from data-tp pass)

  - `1d887bcd` Interactive Map - Dev Revisions: startDate 4/22, endDate 5/7, status in-progress. Spans past today.
  - `05793ebe` QA Phase: startDate 5/7, endDate 5/8. Future multi-day, should anchor only on startDate's day until 5/7.

  ## What I'm asking thought-partner for

  1. Confirm the placement-rule table above matches the design intent, or propose a refinement.
  2. Locate the renderer (likely under `src/app/runway/...` or `src/components/runway/...`) and identify the specific
  function/component doing the day-cell anchoring for `This Week`.
  3. Plan the logic fix: filter the day-cell placement to exclude rows where `startDate <= today`, with the active-span
  sections (Today, In Flight) handling those rows instead.
  4. Surface any second-order effects (sort order, "upcoming" surface, retainer wrapper containers) before CC writes
  code.

  Out of scope for this ticket: any data corrections. The data is right.

  ## Reference rows (so you can hydrate without re-deriving)

  - LPPC client_id: `d27916a0809747f99fe9a8157`
  - Today: 2026-04-29
  - Affected row IDs: `63e4aeab1d6d47449458e9d5b`, `1d887bcd1a044c98bcab83187`, `05793ebe0358492c8f17d0f35`

  Paste-ready. Drops them at the right altitude (placement rules + repro case + reference rows) so they don't have to
  dig.

⏺ Here's the paste-ready thought-partner brief, anchored on the agent's findings:

  # R1 Thought Partner brief: Slack-bot modal trigger for net-new entity creation

  ## What the operator wants

  When someone in Slack DM-converses with the Runway bot in natural language and the bot decides this input means
  "create a NEW retainer wrapper, NEW L1 project, or NEW L2 week_item," surface a Slack modal first. User confirms /
  fills missing fields / cancels in the modal; the write only fires after submit.

  Modal scope: net-new creates only (not updates). Three target entities: wrapper, L1, L2.

  ## Current pipeline (verified from code, file:line refs included)

  ### Intent classification
  - Pure LLM tool-calling via Vercel AI SDK's `generateText`, model `claude-haiku-4-5-20251001`.
  - `src/lib/slack/bot.ts:204-210` — `generateText({ model, messages, tools, stopWhen: stepCountIs(MAX_STEPS=12),
  maxRetries: 1 })`.
  - Slack DM → `/api/slack/events/route.ts:115-125` enqueues Inngest → `inngest/functions/runway-slack-message.ts:48`
  calls `handleDirectMessage` → spawns the LLM tool loop.
  - No regex, no rules-based router, no separate classifier. The model emits `toolCalls` and the dispatch happens inside
   the AI-SDK loop.

  ### Create-vs-update decision
  - Lives entirely in the LLM's prompt-driven choice between `create_*` and `update_*` tool names.
  - The "policy" is text in `src/lib/runway/bot-context-behaviors.ts:67-85,96-125` — confirmation rules, ambiguity
  guidance, "Sound right?" prompt before creating a project — purely instruction to the model, NOT enforced anywhere in
  code.
  - `src/lib/slack/bot.ts:223-238` only LOGS tool calls AFTER they execute. There's no pre-write hook today.

  ### Tool surface (bot-tools.ts)
  | Create-side | Update-side |
  |---|---|
  | `create_project` (line 261) | `update_project_status`, `update_project_field` |
  | `create_week_item` (line 369) | `update_week_item` |
  | `create_pipeline_item` (line 527) | `update_pipeline_item` |
  | `create_team_member` (line 611) | `update_team_member`, `update_client_field` |

  Plus `add_update` (note-only, not a write), `undo_last_change`, three `delete_*`.

  ### Wrapper creation is broken at the bot layer
  - A "wrapper" needs `engagementType="retainer"` + `parentProjectId=null` + child L1s linked.
  - Bot's `create_project` (`bot-tools.ts:264-273`) does NOT expose `engagementType`, `parentProjectId`,
  `contractStart`, or `contractEnd`. It only takes `clientSlug, name, status, owner, resources, dueDate, waitingOn,
  notes`.
  - `update_project_field`'s field enum (`bot-tools.ts:315-323`) excludes `engagementType` entirely.
  - MCP's `add_project` (`runway-tools.ts:512-527`) and the underlying `addProject` operation
  (`operations-add.ts:36-49`) DO expose all the wrapper fields. The bot is the bottleneck.
  - Net effect: the bot literally cannot create a retainer wrapper today. Modal work needs to either fix this gap first
  or accept that "wrapper" is an MCP/data-tp-only path.

  ### Modal scaffolding state
  - ZERO. Grep for `views.open|modal|interactivity|block_actions|view_submission` across `src/` returns no Slack-modal
  hits.
  - No `/api/slack/interactivity` route. Slack signature verification exists in `src/lib/slack/verify.ts` (reusable).
  Slack client at `src/lib/slack/client.ts` is currently used for `chat.postMessage` only.

  ### The hard architectural problem
  - `generateText`'s `execute:` callback inside each `tool({ ... })` definition runs inside the LLM loop. It must
  resolve a result before `generateText` proceeds.
  - A modal-gated flow can't just "pause" the loop and wait for user submit — Vercel AI SDK doesn't support resumable
  tool calls in this shape.
  - Realistic shape: when an `execute` callback for a `create_*` tool fires, it stores the proposed args server-side,
  opens a Slack modal, returns a "modal opened, awaiting confirmation" result to the LLM (which will likely respond to
  user "I've opened a confirmation modal"), and TERMINATES the run. On modal submit, a new `/api/slack/interactivity`
  handler picks up the stored args and invokes the underlying `addProject` / `createWeekItem` directly (bypassing the
  LLM round-trip).

  ### Disambiguation gaps that affect modal scope
  - Per `bot-context-behaviors.ts:80-85`, ambiguity is resolved by prompt instruction (LLM asks). Examples don't cover
  create-vs-update specifically.
  - "Add a follow-up for Convergix" likely defaults to `create_week_item` — no instruction to first search for existing
  matches.
  - `addProject` blocks exact-normalized duplicate names (`operations-add.ts:106`), but close-but-not-equal names would
  slip through.
  - A modal could also be a disambiguation surface: "We found 3 similar existing items. Update one, or create new?"

  ## Design questions for thought-partner

  1. **Architectural shape.** Confirm or refine the proposed flow: `execute` callback for `create_*` opens a modal +
  terminates the LLM run + stores proposed args (where? Inngest event payload, KV, DB row?). On modal submit, a fresh
  handler dispatches the create. Identify the failure modes (what if user dismisses the modal? Where does the
  conversation thread state live? Is there a TTL on stored proposals?).

  2. **Wrapper-creation gap.** Is the right move to (a) extend bot's `create_project` to accept
  `engagementType`/`parentProjectId`/`contractStart`/`contractEnd`, then build the modal on top of the unified tool, OR
  (b) leave wrapper creation as MCP/data-tp-only and skip modal-for-wrapper, OR (c) add a dedicated
  `create_retainer_wrapper` bot tool that is modal-gated by default? Trade-offs?

  3. **Modal as disambiguation gate.** Should the modal trigger ALSO fire when input is ambiguous between create and
  update (e.g., proposes "Update existing X (90% match)" vs "Create new" toggles)? Or strictly net-new only?

  4. **Update path.** Operator scoped this to creates. But are there high-impact UPDATES that should also gate behind a
  modal (status changes on multi-month projects, parent_project_id assignments, contract date changes)? Surface as a
  follow-on, don't fold in.

  5. **Slack interactivity stack.** New route at `/api/slack/interactivity`, signature verify, modal definition format
  (Block Kit), state-passing between LLM proposal and modal submit. Identify reusable parts of existing `bot-tools.ts`
  argument validation so the modal handler shares the same write-path.

  6. **What does "create signal" mean concretely.** The bot today decides `create_*` purely from prompt text. Do you
  want to keep that LLM-driven? Or add a deterministic pre-LLM classifier (regex / keyword / lookup) that flags "this
  looks like a create" before the LLM picks a tool? Implications for false-positive modal pops.

  7. **Confirm the resumable-flow assumption.** I claimed `generateText` can't pause and resume. Verify against current
  AI SDK v6 docs — there may be a streaming-tool-result pattern that allows it. If yes, the architecture changes
  substantially.

  ## Out of scope for this brief
  - Data corrections (data-tp's swimlane).
  - The display-logic bug separately filed (multi-day rows rendering twice).
  - Auth / WorkOS layer changes.
  - Production deployment plan (Runway deploys from runway branch already; no Vercel preview gate).

  ## Reference files (hydration list)
  - `src/lib/slack/bot.ts` — main loop, model config, MAX_STEPS, MUTATION_TOOLS list.
  - `src/lib/slack/bot-tools.ts` — all tool definitions with `execute:` callbacks. Modal injection points live here.
  - `src/lib/runway/bot-context-behaviors.ts` — system-prompt instructions (intent guidance lives here).
  - `src/lib/runway/bot-context.ts`, `bot-context-sections.ts` — system prompt assembly.
  - `src/lib/mcp/runway-tools.ts` — MCP tool registry (compare full surface vs bot's restricted surface).
  - `src/lib/runway/operations-add.ts`, `operations-writes-project.ts` — underlying write helpers (modal handler will
  call these directly post-submit).
  - `src/app/api/slack/events/route.ts` — Slack event ingress, signature verify pattern.
  - `src/lib/inngest/functions/runway-slack-message.ts` — Inngest function that owns the conversation lifecycle.
  - `src/lib/slack/verify.ts` — Slack signature verification helper.
  - `src/lib/slack/client.ts` — Slack Web API client.

  ## What I'm asking for back
  A staged plan: (1) close the wrapper-creation gap, (2) ship `/api/slack/interactivity` infra + a working modal for one
   `create_*` path as proof of pattern, (3) extend to all four create paths + wrapper, (4) optionally extend to
  disambiguation. Each stage with code-level direction CC can act on.

  Paste-ready. Drops thought-partner straight into the architecture seam without re-discovery overhead.

⏺ All 6 warnings are false positives. The detector is checking dayOfWeek and weekOf against startDate when the
  convention (per the intent doc) ties both fields to date, not startDate.

  Verification against prod

  Row: R3 Design Review
  Field: dayOfWeek=thursday
  Prod state: date=4/23 (Thu), startDate=4/20 (Mon)
  Convention check: 4/23 is Thursday → match ✓
  Detector said: "dayOfWeek 'thursday' doesn't match 2026-04-20 (monday)" — checks startDate
  Reality: False positive
  ────────────────────────────────────────
  Row: Development Kickoff
  Field: dayOfWeek=thursday
  Prod state: date=4/23 (Thu), startDate=4/20 (Mon)
  Convention check: Same as above ✓
  Detector said: Same wrong-field check
  Reality: False positive
  ────────────────────────────────────────
  Row: Pencils Down
  Field: dayOfWeek=monday
  Prod state: date=5/4 (Mon), startDate=4/23 (Thu)
  Convention check: 5/4 is Monday → match ✓
  Detector said: "dayOfWeek 'monday' doesn't match 2026-04-23 (thursday)" — checks startDate
  Reality: False positive
  ────────────────────────────────────────
  Row: QA Phase
  Field: dayOfWeek=friday
  Prod state: date=5/8 (Fri), startDate=5/7 (Thu)
  Convention check: 5/8 is Friday → match ✓
  Detector said: "dayOfWeek 'friday' doesn't match 2026-05-07 (thursday)" — checks startDate
  Reality: False positive
  ────────────────────────────────────────
  Row: Pencils Down
  Field: weekOf=2026-05-04
  Prod state: date=5/4, startDate=4/23
  Convention check: Monday(date)=5/4 → match ✓
  Detector said: "weekOf '2026-05-04' isn't Monday-of-week for 2026-04-23 (expected 2026-04-20)" — checks startDate's
    week
  Reality: False positive
  ────────────────────────────────────────
  Row: Policy Materials Import
  Field: weekOf=2026-05-04
  Prod state: date=5/4, startDate=4/27
  Convention check: Monday(date)=5/4 → match ✓
  Detector said: "weekOf '2026-05-04' isn't Monday-of-week for 2026-04-27 (expected 2026-04-27)" — checks startDate's
    week
  Reality: False positive

  Convention reference (intent doc, lines 17-20)

  ▎ date mirrors endDate on multi-day range tasks.
  ▎ dayOfWeek tracks date (not startDate).
  ▎ weekOf is the Monday of the week containing date.

  The mechanical sweep we just ran enforced exactly this — date=endDate, dayOfWeek=Monday-of-date's-day-of-week,
  weekOf=Monday(date). Every row the Gantt flagged is convention-clean.

  Why the detector is wrong

  The Gantt TP's detector is reading startDate as the anchor for dayOfWeek and weekOf checks. That would be correct
  under a different convention ("dayOfWeek tracks startDate") but the project picked the opposite — date is the
  canonical anchor for both, and date == endDate on multi-day items.

  For single-day rows (startDate == date == endDate) the detector accidentally produces correct results because all
  three fields agree. The bug only surfaces on multi-day items — which is exactly what the Gantt is showing.

  Fix direction (when you brief the Gantt TP)

  Detector check should be:

  const expectedDayOfWeek = dayName(row.date);          // not row.startDate
  const expectedWeekOf = mondayOf(row.date);            // not mondayOf(row.startDate)

  And the convention reference for whoever owns it: docs/runway-data-integrity-intent.md lines 17-20.

  Other observations from the Gantt

  The visual itself is clean — milestones (LPPC Images Due, Hero Video Resolution, Staging Links Due, etc.) render
  correctly as diamonds. Active multi-day bars (Pencils Down 4/23-5/4, Policy Materials Import 4/27-5/4, QA Phase
  5/7-5/8) render correctly. The display layer is doing the right thing; only the integrity detector is mis-aligned.

  LPPC Website Revamp data is clean — the Gantt's "5 of 12 rows have data gaps" is a false alarm.

  The row is a faithful multi-day representation. Per Kathy's 2026-04-28 audit, work began ~4/24 (policy materials added
  to CMS) and continues through 5/4 (Leslie tagging in CMS). Current shape:

  - `startDate` = 2026-04-27
  - `date` = 2026-05-04
  - `endDate` = 2026-05-04
  - `weekOf` = 2026-05-04
  - `dayOfWeek` = monday
  - `category` = kickoff
  - `status` = in-progress

  Convention is satisfied: multi-day, `date` mirrors `endDate`, `weekOf` is Monday of date's week. No data correction
  needed.

  ## The bug is in the renderer

  The board's `This Week` section appears to anchor multi-day items on their `startDate`'s day cell. Once `startDate <=
  today`, the row should leave the day-anchored `This Week` placement and live in active-state sections only. That isn't
  happening. Net effect: every multi-day row that crosses today renders twice.

  This affects more than just LPPC. Any active multi-day L2 across the system has the same artifact.

  ## Desired behavior

  Three placement zones, mutually exclusive for a given row at a given point in time:

  | Zone | Match rule |
  |---|---|
  | **Today** | `startDate <= today <= endDate` AND `status != completed/canceled` |
  | **In Flight** | Same condition as Today, but for the broader "what's actively spanning" surface (likely the same set,
   different visual treatment) |
  | **This Week** day cells | Single-day rows where `date == today's week` AND status is scheduled, OR multi-day rows
  where `startDate > today` (haven't started yet, anchored on startDate's day for forecast visibility) |

  Once `startDate` has passed, the day-anchored `This Week` row disappears. Replaced by Today + In Flight presence.

  Future-dated multi-day rows still anchor on startDate's day in `This Week` — so users can see "kickoff Wed of next
  week" before the work starts. The disappearance trigger is `startDate <= today`.

  Pull `Policy Materials Import (LPPC)` weekItem from prod. Render the board. Observe duplicate placement: Mon 4/27 in

  past-startDate.

  # R1 Thought Partner brief: Slack-bot modal trigger for net-new entity creation

  ## What the operator wants

  When someone in Slack DM-converses with the Runway bot in natural language and the bot decides this input means "create
   a NEW retainer wrapper, NEW L1 project, or NEW L2 week_item," surface a Slack modal first. User confirms / fills
  missing fields / cancels in the modal; the write only fires after submit.

  Modal scope: net-new creates only (not updates). Three target entities: wrapper, L1, L2.

  ## Current pipeline (verified from code, file:line refs included)

  ### Intent classification
  - Pure LLM tool-calling via Vercel AI SDK's `generateText`, model `claude-haiku-4-5-20251001`.
  - `src/lib/slack/bot.ts:204-210` — `generateText({ model, messages, tools, stopWhen: stepCountIs(MAX_STEPS=12),
  maxRetries: 1 })`.
  - Slack DM → `/api/slack/events/route.ts:115-125` enqueues Inngest → `inngest/functions/runway-slack-message.ts:48`
  calls `handleDirectMessage` → spawns the LLM tool loop.
  - No regex, no rules-based router, no separate classifier. The model emits `toolCalls` and the dispatch happens inside
  the AI-SDK loop.

  ### Create-vs-update decision
  - Lives entirely in the LLM's prompt-driven choice between `create_*` and `update_*` tool names.
  - The "policy" is text in `src/lib/runway/bot-context-behaviors.ts:67-85,96-125` — confirmation rules, ambiguity
  guidance, "Sound right?" prompt before creating a project — purely instruction to the model, NOT enforced anywhere in
  code.
  - `src/lib/slack/bot.ts:223-238` only LOGS tool calls AFTER they execute. There's no pre-write hook today.

  ### Tool surface (bot-tools.ts)
  | Create-side | Update-side |
  |---|---|
  | `create_project` (line 261) | `update_project_status`, `update_project_field` |
  | `create_week_item` (line 369) | `update_week_item` |
  | `create_pipeline_item` (line 527) | `update_pipeline_item` |
  | `create_team_member` (line 611) | `update_team_member`, `update_client_field` |

  Plus `add_update` (note-only, not a write), `undo_last_change`, three `delete_*`.

  ### Wrapper creation is broken at the bot layer
  - A "wrapper" needs `engagementType="retainer"` + `parentProjectId=null` + child L1s linked.
  - Bot's `create_project` (`bot-tools.ts:264-273`) does NOT expose `engagementType`, `parentProjectId`, `contractStart`,
   or `contractEnd`. It only takes `clientSlug, name, status, owner, resources, dueDate, waitingOn, notes`.
  - `update_project_field`'s field enum (`bot-tools.ts:315-323`) excludes `engagementType` entirely.
  - MCP's `add_project` (`runway-tools.ts:512-527`) and the underlying `addProject` operation (`operations-add.ts:36-49`)
   DO expose all the wrapper fields. The bot is the bottleneck.
  - Net effect: the bot literally cannot create a retainer wrapper today. Modal work needs to either fix this gap first
  or accept that "wrapper" is an MCP/data-tp-only path.

  ### Modal scaffolding state
  - ZERO. Grep for `views.open|modal|interactivity|block_actions|view_submission` across `src/` returns no Slack-modal
  hits.
  - No `/api/slack/interactivity` route. Slack signature verification exists in `src/lib/slack/verify.ts` (reusable).
  Slack client at `src/lib/slack/client.ts` is currently used for `chat.postMessage` only.

  ### The hard architectural problem
  - `generateText`'s `execute:` callback inside each `tool({ ... })` definition runs inside the LLM loop. It must resolve
   a result before `generateText` proceeds.
  - A modal-gated flow can't just "pause" the loop and wait for user submit — Vercel AI SDK doesn't support resumable
  tool calls in this shape.
  - Realistic shape: when an `execute` callback for a `create_*` tool fires, it stores the proposed args server-side,
  opens a Slack modal, returns a "modal opened, awaiting confirmation" result to the LLM (which will likely respond to
  user "I've opened a confirmation modal"), and TERMINATES the run. On modal submit, a new `/api/slack/interactivity`
  handler picks up the stored args and invokes the underlying `addProject` / `createWeekItem` directly (bypassing the LLM
   round-trip).

  ### Disambiguation gaps that affect modal scope
  - Per `bot-context-behaviors.ts:80-85`, ambiguity is resolved by prompt instruction (LLM asks). Examples don't cover
  create-vs-update specifically.
  - "Add a follow-up for Convergix" likely defaults to `create_week_item` — no instruction to first search for existing
  matches.
  - `addProject` blocks exact-normalized duplicate names (`operations-add.ts:106`), but close-but-not-equal names would
  slip through.
  - A modal could also be a disambiguation surface: "We found 3 similar existing items. Update one, or create new?"

  ## Design questions for thought-partner

  1. **Architectural shape.** Confirm or refine the proposed flow: `execute` callback for `create_*` opens a modal +
  terminates the LLM run + stores proposed args (where? Inngest event payload, KV, DB row?). On modal submit, a fresh
  handler dispatches the create. Identify the failure modes (what if user dismisses the modal? Where does the
  conversation thread state live? Is there a TTL on stored proposals?).

  2. **Wrapper-creation gap.** Is the right move to (a) extend bot's `create_project` to accept
  `engagementType`/`parentProjectId`/`contractStart`/`contractEnd`, then build the modal on top of the unified tool, OR
  (b) leave wrapper creation as MCP/data-tp-only and skip modal-for-wrapper, OR (c) add a dedicated
  `create_retainer_wrapper` bot tool that is modal-gated by default? Trade-offs?

  3. **Modal as disambiguation gate.** Should the modal trigger ALSO fire when input is ambiguous between create and
  update (e.g., proposes "Update existing X (90% match)" vs "Create new" toggles)? Or strictly net-new only?

  4. **Update path.** Operator scoped this to creates. But are there high-impact UPDATES that should also gate behind a
  modal (status changes on multi-month projects, parent_project_id assignments, contract date changes)? Surface as a
  follow-on, don't fold in.

  5. **Slack interactivity stack.** New route at `/api/slack/interactivity`, signature verify, modal definition format
  (Block Kit), state-passing between LLM proposal and modal submit. Identify reusable parts of existing `bot-tools.ts`
  argument validation so the modal handler shares the same write-path.

  6. **What does "create signal" mean concretely.** The bot today decides `create_*` purely from prompt text. Do you want
   to keep that LLM-driven? Or add a deterministic pre-LLM classifier (regex / keyword / lookup) that flags "this looks
  like a create" before the LLM picks a tool? Implications for false-positive modal pops.

  7. **Confirm the resumable-flow assumption.** I claimed `generateText` can't pause and resume. Verify against current
  AI SDK v6 docs — there may be a streaming-tool-result pattern that allows it. If yes, the architecture changes
  substantially.

  ## Out of scope for this brief
  - Data corrections (data-tp's swimlane).
  - The display-logic bug separately filed (multi-day rows rendering twice).
  - Auth / WorkOS layer changes.
  - Production deployment plan (Runway deploys from runway branch already; no Vercel preview gate).

  ## Reference files (hydration list)
  - `src/lib/slack/bot.ts` — main loop, model config, MAX_STEPS, MUTATION_TOOLS list.
  - `src/lib/slack/bot-tools.ts` — all tool definitions with `execute:` callbacks. Modal injection points live here.
  - `src/lib/runway/bot-context-behaviors.ts` — system-prompt instructions (intent guidance lives here).
  - `src/lib/runway/bot-context.ts`, `bot-context-sections.ts` — system prompt assembly.
  - `src/lib/mcp/runway-tools.ts` — MCP tool registry (compare full surface vs bot's restricted surface).
  - `src/lib/runway/operations-add.ts`, `operations-writes-project.ts` — underlying write helpers (modal handler will
  call these directly post-submit).
  - `src/app/api/slack/events/route.ts` — Slack event ingress, signature verify pattern.
  - `src/lib/inngest/functions/runway-slack-message.ts` — Inngest function that owns the conversation lifecycle.
  - `src/lib/slack/verify.ts` — Slack signature verification helper.
  - `src/lib/slack/client.ts` — Slack Web API client.

  ## What I'm asking for back
  A staged plan: (1) close the wrapper-creation gap, (2) ship `/api/slack/interactivity` infra + a working modal for one
  `create_*` path as proof of pattern, (3) extend to all four create paths + wrapper, (4) optionally extend to
  disambiguation. Each stage with code-level direction CC can act on.

  Paste-ready. Drops thought-partner straight into the architecture seam without re-discovery overhead.

⏺ All 6 warnings are false positives. The detector is checking dayOfWeek and weekOf against startDate when the convention
   (per the intent doc) ties both fields to date, not startDate.

  Verification against prod

  Row: R3 Design Review
  Field: dayOfWeek=thursday
  Prod state: date=4/23 (Thu), startDate=4/20 (Mon)
  Convention check: 4/23 is Thursday → match ✓
  Detector said: "dayOfWeek 'thursday' doesn't match 2026-04-20 (monday)" — checks startDate
  Reality: False positive
  ────────────────────────────────────────
  Row: Development Kickoff
  Field: dayOfWeek=thursday
  Prod state: date=4/23 (Thu), startDate=4/20 (Mon)
  Convention check: Same as above ✓
  Detector said: Same wrong-field check
  Reality: False positive
  ────────────────────────────────────────
  Row: Pencils Down
  Field: dayOfWeek=monday
  Prod state: date=5/4 (Mon), startDate=4/23 (Thu)
  Convention check: 5/4 is Monday → match ✓
  Detector said: "dayOfWeek 'monday' doesn't match 2026-04-23 (thursday)" — checks startDate
  Reality: False positive
  ────────────────────────────────────────
  Row: QA Phase
  Field: dayOfWeek=friday
  Prod state: date=5/8 (Fri), startDate=5/7 (Thu)
  Convention check: 5/8 is Friday → match ✓
  Detector said: "dayOfWeek 'friday' doesn't match 2026-05-07 (thursday)" — checks startDate
  Reality: False positive
  ────────────────────────────────────────
  Row: Pencils Down
  Field: weekOf=2026-05-04
  Prod state: date=5/4, startDate=4/23
  Convention check: Monday(date)=5/4 → match ✓
  Detector said: "weekOf '2026-05-04' isn't Monday-of-week for 2026-04-23 (expected 2026-04-20)" — checks startDate's
  week
  Reality: False positive
  ────────────────────────────────────────
  Row: Policy Materials Import
  Field: weekOf=2026-05-04
  Prod state: date=5/4, startDate=4/27
  Convention check: Monday(date)=5/4 → match ✓
  Detector said: "weekOf '2026-05-04' isn't Monday-of-week for 2026-04-27 (expected 2026-04-27)" — checks startDate's
  week
  Reality: False positive

  Convention reference (intent doc, lines 17-20)

  ▎ date mirrors endDate on multi-day range tasks.
  ▎ dayOfWeek tracks date (not startDate).
  ▎ weekOf is the Monday of the week containing date.

  The mechanical sweep we just ran enforced exactly this — date=endDate, dayOfWeek=Monday-of-date's-day-of-week,
  weekOf=Monday(date). Every row the Gantt flagged is convention-clean.

  Why the detector is wrong

  The Gantt TP's detector is reading startDate as the anchor for dayOfWeek and weekOf checks. That would be correct under
   a different convention ("dayOfWeek tracks startDate") but the project picked the opposite — date is the canonical
  anchor for both, and date == endDate on multi-day items.

  For single-day rows (startDate == date == endDate) the detector accidentally produces correct results because all three
   fields agree. The bug only surfaces on multi-day items — which is exactly what the Gantt is showing.

  Fix direction (when you brief the Gantt TP)

  Detector check should be:

  const expectedDayOfWeek = dayName(row.date);          // not row.startDate
  const expectedWeekOf = mondayOf(row.date);            // not mondayOf(row.startDate)

  And the convention reference for whoever owns it: docs/runway-data-integrity-intent.md lines 17-20.

  Other observations from the Gantt

  The visual itself is clean — milestones (LPPC Images Due, Hero Video Resolution, Staging Links Due, etc.) render
  correctly as diamonds. Active multi-day bars (Pencils Down 4/23-5/4, Policy Materials Import 4/27-5/4, QA Phase
  5/7-5/8) render correctly. The display layer is doing the right thing; only the integrity detector is mis-aligned.

  LPPC Website Revamp data is clean — the Gantt's "5 of 12 rows have data gaps" is a false alarm.

⏺ # Runway display-logic gap: multi-day rows render twice

  ## What I observed

  `Policy Materials Import (LPPC)` (id `63e4aeab1d6d47449458e9d5b`) appears in two places on the board today:

  1. Under `This Week` -> `Mon 4/27` — placed by `startDate=2026-04-27`
  2. Presumably also under In Flight / Today — placed because the row is actively spanning today

  Same row, same data, two visual locations. Confirmed via screenshot from the board.

  ## Data state is correct

  The row is a faithful multi-day representation. Per Kathy's 2026-04-28 audit, work began ~4/24 (policy materials added
  to CMS) and continues through 5/4 (Leslie tagging in CMS). Current shape:

  - `startDate` = 2026-04-27
  - `date` = 2026-05-04
  - `endDate` = 2026-05-04
  - `weekOf` = 2026-05-04
  - `dayOfWeek` = monday
  - `category` = kickoff
  - `status` = in-progress

  Convention is satisfied: multi-day, `date` mirrors `endDate`, `weekOf` is Monday of date's week. No data correction
  needed.

  ## The bug is in the renderer

  The board's `This Week` section appears to anchor multi-day items on their `startDate`'s day cell. Once `startDate <=
  today`, the row should leave the day-anchored `This Week` placement and live in active-state sections only. That isn't
  happening. Net effect: every multi-day row that crosses today renders twice.

  This affects more than just LPPC. Any active multi-day L2 across the system has the same artifact.

  ## Desired behavior

  Three placement zones, mutually exclusive for a given row at a given point in time:

  | Zone | Match rule |
  |---|---|
  | **Today** | `startDate <= today <= endDate` AND `status != completed/canceled` |
  | **In Flight** | Same condition as Today, but for the broader "what's actively spanning" surface (likely the same set,
   different visual treatment) |
  | **This Week** day cells | Single-day rows where `date == today's week` AND status is scheduled, OR multi-day rows
  where `startDate > today` (haven't started yet, anchored on startDate's day for forecast visibility) |

  Once `startDate` has passed, the day-anchored `This Week` row disappears. Replaced by Today + In Flight presence.

  Future-dated multi-day rows still anchor on startDate's day in `This Week` — so users can see "kickoff Wed of next
  week" before the work starts. The disappearance trigger is `startDate <= today`.

  ## Repro case

  Pull `Policy Materials Import (LPPC)` weekItem from prod. Render the board. Observe duplicate placement: Mon 4/27 in
  `This Week` AND wherever active spans render. Today is 2026-04-29, startDate is 2026-04-27, so the row is
  past-startDate.

  After fix, the Mon 4/27 placement should be gone; only Today + In Flight render this row.

  ## Other multi-day rows likely affected (LPPC scope, fresh from data-tp pass)

  - `1d887bcd` Interactive Map - Dev Revisions: startDate 4/22, endDate 5/7, status in-progress. Spans past today.
  - `05793ebe` QA Phase: startDate 5/7, endDate 5/8. Future multi-day, should anchor only on startDate's day until 5/7.

  ## What I'm asking thought-partner for

  1. Confirm the placement-rule table above matches the design intent, or propose a refinement.
  2. Locate the renderer (likely under `src/app/runway/...` or `src/components/runway/...`) and identify the specific
  function/component doing the day-cell anchoring for `This Week`.
  3. Plan the logic fix: filter the day-cell placement to exclude rows where `startDate <= today`, with the active-span
  sections (Today, In Flight) handling those rows instead.
  4. Surface any second-order effects (sort order, "upcoming" surface, retainer wrapper containers) before CC writes
  code.

  Out of scope for this ticket: any data corrections. The data is right.

  # R1 Thought Partner brief: Slack-bot modal trigger for net-new entity creation

  ## What the operator wants

  When someone in Slack DM-converses with the Runway bot in natural language and the bot decides this input means "create
   a NEW retainer wrapper, NEW L1 project, or NEW L2 week_item," surface a Slack modal first. User confirms / fills
  missing fields / cancels in the modal; the write only fires after submit.

  Modal scope: net-new creates only (not updates). Three target entities: wrapper, L1, L2.

  ## Current pipeline (verified from code, file:line refs included)

  ### Intent classification
  - Pure LLM tool-calling via Vercel AI SDK's `generateText`, model `claude-haiku-4-5-20251001`.
  - `src/lib/slack/bot.ts:204-210` — `generateText({ model, messages, tools, stopWhen: stepCountIs(MAX_STEPS=12),
  maxRetries: 1 })`.
  - Slack DM → `/api/slack/events/route.ts:115-125` enqueues Inngest → `inngest/functions/runway-slack-message.ts:48`
  calls `handleDirectMessage` → spawns the LLM tool loop.
  - No regex, no rules-based router, no separate classifier. The model emits `toolCalls` and the dispatch happens inside
  the AI-SDK loop.

  ### Create-vs-update decision
  - Lives entirely in the LLM's prompt-driven choice between `create_*` and `update_*` tool names.
  - The "policy" is text in `src/lib/runway/bot-context-behaviors.ts:67-85,96-125` — confirmation rules, ambiguity
  guidance, "Sound right?" prompt before creating a project — purely instruction to the model, NOT enforced anywhere in
  code.
  - `src/lib/slack/bot.ts:223-238` only LOGS tool calls AFTER they execute. There's no pre-write hook today.

  ### Tool surface (bot-tools.ts)
  | Create-side | Update-side |
  |---|---|
  | `create_project` (line 261) | `update_project_status`, `update_project_field` |
  | `create_week_item` (line 369) | `update_week_item` |
  | `create_pipeline_item` (line 527) | `update_pipeline_item` |
  | `create_team_member` (line 611) | `update_team_member`, `update_client_field` |

  Plus `add_update` (note-only, not a write), `undo_last_change`, three `delete_*`.

  ### Wrapper creation is broken at the bot layer
  - A "wrapper" needs `engagementType="retainer"` + `parentProjectId=null` + child L1s linked.
  - Bot's `create_project` (`bot-tools.ts:264-273`) does NOT expose `engagementType`, `parentProjectId`, `contractStart`,
   or `contractEnd`. It only takes `clientSlug, name, status, owner, resources, dueDate, waitingOn, notes`.
  - `update_project_field`'s field enum (`bot-tools.ts:315-323`) excludes `engagementType` entirely.
  - MCP's `add_project` (`runway-tools.ts:512-527`) and the underlying `addProject` operation (`operations-add.ts:36-49`)
   DO expose all the wrapper fields. The bot is the bottleneck.
  - Net effect: the bot literally cannot create a retainer wrapper today. Modal work needs to either fix this gap first
  or accept that "wrapper" is an MCP/data-tp-only path.

  ### Modal scaffolding state
  - ZERO. Grep for `views.open|modal|interactivity|block_actions|view_submission` across `src/` returns no Slack-modal
  hits.
  - No `/api/slack/interactivity` route. Slack signature verification exists in `src/lib/slack/verify.ts` (reusable).
  Slack client at `src/lib/slack/client.ts` is currently used for `chat.postMessage` only.

  ### The hard architectural problem
  - `generateText`'s `execute:` callback inside each `tool({ ... })` definition runs inside the LLM loop. It must resolve
   a result before `generateText` proceeds.
  - A modal-gated flow can't just "pause" the loop and wait for user submit — Vercel AI SDK doesn't support resumable
  tool calls in this shape.
  - Realistic shape: when an `execute` callback for a `create_*` tool fires, it stores the proposed args server-side,
  opens a Slack modal, returns a "modal opened, awaiting confirmation" result to the LLM (which will likely respond to
  user "I've opened a confirmation modal"), and TERMINATES the run. On modal submit, a new `/api/slack/interactivity`
  handler picks up the stored args and invokes the underlying `addProject` / `createWeekItem` directly (bypassing the LLM
   round-trip).

  ### Disambiguation gaps that affect modal scope
  - Per `bot-context-behaviors.ts:80-85`, ambiguity is resolved by prompt instruction (LLM asks). Examples don't cover
  create-vs-update specifically.
  - "Add a follow-up for Convergix" likely defaults to `create_week_item` — no instruction to first search for existing
  matches.
  - `addProject` blocks exact-normalized duplicate names (`operations-add.ts:106`), but close-but-not-equal names would
  slip through.
  - A modal could also be a disambiguation surface: "We found 3 similar existing items. Update one, or create new?"

  ## Design questions for thought-partner

  1. **Architectural shape.** Confirm or refine the proposed flow: `execute` callback for `create_*` opens a modal +
  terminates the LLM run + stores proposed args (where? Inngest event payload, KV, DB row?). On modal submit, a fresh
  handler dispatches the create. Identify the failure modes (what if user dismisses the modal? Where does the
  conversation thread state live? Is there a TTL on stored proposals?).

  2. **Wrapper-creation gap.** Is the right move to (a) extend bot's `create_project` to accept
  `engagementType`/`parentProjectId`/`contractStart`/`contractEnd`, then build the modal on top of the unified tool, OR
  (b) leave wrapper creation as MCP/data-tp-only and skip modal-for-wrapper, OR (c) add a dedicated
  `create_retainer_wrapper` bot tool that is modal-gated by default? Trade-offs?

  3. **Modal as disambiguation gate.** Should the modal trigger ALSO fire when input is ambiguous between create and
  update (e.g., proposes "Update existing X (90% match)" vs "Create new" toggles)? Or strictly net-new only?

  4. **Update path.** Operator scoped this to creates. But are there high-impact UPDATES that should also gate behind a
  modal (status changes on multi-month projects, parent_project_id assignments, contract date changes)? Surface as a
  follow-on, don't fold in.

  5. **Slack interactivity stack.** New route at `/api/slack/interactivity`, signature verify, modal definition format
  (Block Kit), state-passing between LLM proposal and modal submit. Identify reusable parts of existing `bot-tools.ts`
  argument validation so the modal handler shares the same write-path.

  6. **What does "create signal" mean concretely.** The bot today decides `create_*` purely from prompt text. Do you want
   to keep that LLM-driven? Or add a deterministic pre-LLM classifier (regex / keyword / lookup) that flags "this looks
  like a create" before the LLM picks a tool? Implications for false-positive modal pops.

  7. **Confirm the resumable-flow assumption.** I claimed `generateText` can't pause and resume. Verify against current
  AI SDK v6 docs — there may be a streaming-tool-result pattern that allows it. If yes, the architecture changes
  substantially.

  ## Out of scope for this brief
  - Data corrections (data-tp's swimlane).
  - The display-logic bug separately filed (multi-day rows rendering twice).
  - Auth / WorkOS layer changes.
  - Production deployment plan (Runway deploys from runway branch already; no Vercel preview gate).

  ## Reference files (hydration list)
  - `src/lib/slack/bot.ts` — main loop, model config, MAX_STEPS, MUTATION_TOOLS list.
  - `src/lib/slack/bot-tools.ts` — all tool definitions with `execute:` callbacks. Modal injection points live here.
  - `src/lib/runway/bot-context-behaviors.ts` — system-prompt instructions (intent guidance lives here).
  - `src/lib/runway/bot-context.ts`, `bot-context-sections.ts` — system prompt assembly.
  - `src/lib/mcp/runway-tools.ts` — MCP tool registry (compare full surface vs bot's restricted surface).
  - `src/lib/runway/operations-add.ts`, `operations-writes-project.ts` — underlying write helpers (modal handler will
  call these directly post-submit).
  - `src/app/api/slack/events/route.ts` — Slack event ingress, signature verify pattern.
  - `src/lib/inngest/functions/runway-slack-message.ts` — Inngest function that owns the conversation lifecycle.
  - `src/lib/slack/verify.ts` — Slack signature verification helper.
  - `src/lib/slack/client.ts` — Slack Web API client.

  ## What I'm asking for back
  A staged plan: (1) close the wrapper-creation gap, (2) ship `/api/slack/interactivity` infra + a working modal for one
  `create_*` path as proof of pattern, (3) extend to all four create paths + wrapper, (4) optionally extend to
  disambiguation. Each stage with code-level direction CC can act on.

  Paste-ready. Drops thought-partner straight into the architecture seam without re-discovery overhead.

  week

  Row: Policy Materials Import
  Field: weekOf=2026-05-04
  Prod state: date=5/4, startDate=4/27
  Convention check: Monday(date)=5/4 → match ✓
  Detector said: "weekOf '2026-05-04' isn't Monday-of-week for 2026-04-27 (expected 2026-04-27)" — checks startDate's
  week
  Reality: False positive

  Convention reference (intent doc, lines 17-20)

  ▎ date mirrors endDate on multi-day range tasks.
  ▎ dayOfWeek tracks date (not startDate).
  ▎ weekOf is the Monday of the week containing date.

  The mechanical sweep we just ran enforced exactly this — date=endDate, dayOfWeek=Monday-of-date's-day-of-week,
  weekOf=Monday(date). Every row the Gantt flagged is convention-clean.

  Why the detector is wrong

  The Gantt TP's detector is reading startDate as the anchor for dayOfWeek and weekOf checks. That would be correct under
   a different convention ("dayOfWeek tracks startDate") but the project picked the opposite — date is the canonical
  anchor for both, and date == endDate on multi-day items.

  For single-day rows (startDate == date == endDate) the detector accidentally produces correct results because all three
   fields agree. The bug only surfaces on multi-day items — which is exactly what the Gantt is showing.

  Fix direction (when you brief the Gantt TP)

  Detector check should be:

  const expectedDayOfWeek = dayName(row.date);          // not row.startDate
  const expectedWeekOf = mondayOf(row.date);            // not mondayOf(row.startDate)

  And the convention reference for whoever owns it: docs/runway-data-integrity-intent.md lines 17-20.

  Other observations from the Gantt

  The visual itself is clean — milestones (LPPC Images Due, Hero Video Resolution, Staging Links Due, etc.) render
  correctly as diamonds. Active multi-day bars (Pencils Down 4/23-5/4, Policy Materials Import 4/27-5/4, QA Phase
  5/7-5/8) render correctly. The display layer is doing the right thing; only the integrity detector is mis-aligned.

  LPPC Website Revamp data is clean — the Gantt's "5 of 12 rows have data gaps" is a false alarm.

⏺ # Runway display-logic gap: multi-day rows render twice

  ## What I observed

  `Policy Materials Import (LPPC)` (id `63e4aeab1d6d47449458e9d5b`) appears in two places on the board today:

  1. Under `This Week` -> `Mon 4/27` — placed by `startDate=2026-04-27`
  2. Presumably also under In Flight / Today — placed because the row is actively spanning today

  Same row, same data, two visual locations. Confirmed via screenshot from the board.

  ## Data state is correct

  The row is a faithful multi-day representation. Per Kathy's 2026-04-28 audit, work began ~4/24 (policy materials added
   to CMS) and continues through 5/4 (Leslie tagging in CMS). Current shape:

  - `startDate` = 2026-04-27
  - `date` = 2026-05-04
  - `endDate` = 2026-05-04
  - `weekOf` = 2026-05-04
  - `dayOfWeek` = monday
  - `category` = kickoff
  - `status` = in-progress

  Convention is satisfied: multi-day, `date` mirrors `endDate`, `weekOf` is Monday of date's week. No data correction
  needed.

  ## The bug is in the renderer

  The board's `This Week` section appears to anchor multi-day items on their `startDate`'s day cell. Once `startDate <=
  today`, the row should leave the day-anchored `This Week` placement and live in active-state sections only. That isn't
   happening. Net effect: every multi-day row that crosses today renders twice.

  This affects more than just LPPC. Any active multi-day L2 across the system has the same artifact.

  ## Desired behavior

  Three placement zones, mutually exclusive for a given row at a given point in time:

  | Zone | Match rule |
  |---|---|
  | **Today** | `startDate <= today <= endDate` AND `status != completed/canceled` |
  | **In Flight** | Same condition as Today, but for the broader "what's actively spanning" surface (likely the same
  set, different visual treatment) |
  | **This Week** day cells | Single-day rows where `date == today's week` AND status is scheduled, OR multi-day rows
  where `startDate > today` (haven't started yet, anchored on startDate's day for forecast visibility) |

  Once `startDate` has passed, the day-anchored `This Week` row disappears. Replaced by Today + In Flight presence.

  Future-dated multi-day rows still anchor on startDate's day in `This Week` — so users can see "kickoff Wed of next
  week" before the work starts. The disappearance trigger is `startDate <= today`.

  ## Repro case

  Pull `Policy Materials Import (LPPC)` weekItem from prod. Render the board. Observe duplicate placement: Mon 4/27 in
  `This Week` AND wherever active spans render. Today is 2026-04-29, startDate is 2026-04-27, so the row is
  past-startDate.

  After fix, the Mon 4/27 placement should be gone; only Today + In Flight render this row.

  ## Other multi-day rows likely affected (LPPC scope, fresh from data-tp pass)

  - `1d887bcd` Interactive Map - Dev Revisions: startDate 4/22, endDate 5/7, status in-progress. Spans past today.
  - `05793ebe` QA Phase: startDate 5/7, endDate 5/8. Future multi-day, should anchor only on startDate's day until 5/7.

  ## What I'm asking thought-partner for

  1. Confirm the placement-rule table above matches the design intent, or propose a refinement.
  2. Locate the renderer (likely under `src/app/runway/...` or `src/components/runway/...`) and identify the specific
  function/component doing the day-cell anchoring for `This Week`.
  3. Plan the logic fix: filter the day-cell placement to exclude rows where `startDate <= today`, with the active-span
  sections (Today, In Flight) handling those rows instead.
  4. Surface any second-order effects (sort order, "upcoming" surface, retainer wrapper containers) before CC writes
  code.

  Out of scope for this ticket: any data corrections. The data is right.

  ## Reference rows (so you can hydrate without re-deriving)

  - LPPC client_id: `d27916a0809747f99fe9a8157`
  - Today: 2026-04-29
  - Affected row IDs: `63e4aeab1d6d47449458e9d5b`, `1d887bcd1a044c98bcab83187`, `05793ebe0358492c8f17d0f35`

  Paste-ready. Drops them at the right altitude (placement rules + repro case + reference rows) so they don't have to
  dig.
